The best trolling motor battery setup for most fishing boats is a dedicated LiFePO4 (lithium iron phosphate) battery system, sized to your trolling motor's voltage and how long you fish.

Lithium is generally the best choice because it's lighter than lead-acid, provides more usable capacity, maintains voltage better under load, and lasts significantly longer.

Best setups by trolling motor voltage

Motor voltage

	

Recommended battery setup

	

Best for




12V

24V

	

2 × 12V 100Ah in series, or 1 × 24V 100Ah

	

Most bass boats




36V

	

3 × 12V 100Ah in series, or 1 × 36V 100Ah

	

Larger bass boats, high-thrust motors

For all-day fishing, 100Ah is a strong starting point. If you regularly use Spot-Lock, fish in strong currents, or run the motor hard, consider 125–150Ah or more.

My preferred configuration: A dedicated 24V or 36V LiFePO4 battery, paired with a compatible lithium charger, a correctly sized circuit breaker, and marine-grade wiring. A single battery simplifies wiring, although multiple 12V batteries offer more flexibility when replacing individual units.

The best trolling motor battery setup for most fishing boats is a dedicated LiFePO4 lithium battery system, separate from the engine's starting battery.

For 24V and 36V motors, a single purpose-built 24V or 36V lithium battery is also an excellent option. It simplifies wiring and reduces the number of connections.

My preferred setup: LiFePO4 batteries, a compatible onboard charger, a properly sized circuit breaker, marine-grade wiring, and a separate starting battery.

Important installation details

Battery management: Choose a BMS with sufficient continuous current and surge capability for your motor.

Charging: Use a LiFePO4-compatible charger matched to the bank voltage and configuration.

Protection: Install a marine-rated circuit breaker sized for your motor and wiring.

Wiring: Use tinned marine-grade copper wire, sized for the current and cable length.

Compatibility: Confirm your motor supports the lithium battery's operating voltage range, and that batteries are approved for series wiring if applicable.
